page.layout: One page of text, with a running head at the top, a centred subheading line below a rule, then one column of verse. A catchword sits at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.p:
Quicunque terras incolunt:
Fama urbis Solymæ quorum pervenit ad aures,
Vetusque Gentis gloria,
Illo nor unquam superari posse putabant
Ab hoste tanta mœnia.
Nulliusque unquam tantas conatibus arces,
Portasque posse deici.
main_text.head: MEM. NVN. SAMECH.
main_text.p:
NVTV qui facili cuncta Deus regit
Gentis turpe suæ crimen, & impia
Vatis somnia vani
Pœnis talibus arguit.

Tali sacrilegas Pontificum manus
Inuisumque nefas supplicio eluit:
Quæ fudere per urbis
Iustum compita sanguinem.

Nam cunctas Solymæ polluerant domos
Cædes, impietas, perfidia & doli.
Labes putida cunctas
Vestes commaculauerat.

Tunc edicta Dei quis veritus sacra
Vicinis timuit sordibus infici?
Quis contagia fugit,
Et passim scelus obuium?

Cassus lumine sic, quum vagus ambulat,
Non vitat salebras, non pedibus cauet:

page.notes: The page is set in roman with italic verse. The opening stanza is a continuation from the previous page and is set in italic. The heading "MEM. NVN. SAMECH." is a Hebrew-letter division, transcribed as printed. The first word of the stanza, "NVTV", is a large woodcut initial "N" joined to the following capitals. The word "Cautes" at the lower right is the catchword. The Latin "Vetusque" and "Portasque" are printed as shown. Uncertain readings: none marked. "Illo nor" is printed with "nor" as shown.
